html:
The United States has completed its withdrawal from Iraq, 23 years after President George W. Bush's "shock and awe" campaign, marking a significant reorientation of US military engagement in the region. This withdrawal comes as the US expands its military presence around Iran and President Trump suggests a US-Iran war could end "very soon."

Russia-Ukraine: The conflict in Ukraine continues to escalate, with Russia hitting a second major bridge in Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge, following repeated attacks on another key bridge. In response, Zelenskiy of Ukraine stated that Ukraine will hit Russian refineries as part of a response to Moscow's "new doctrine" of airstrikes.

US-Iran Tensions: Amid the US military reorientation, the US is expanding its military presence around Iran, deploying three aircraft carriers and up to 10,000 more troops. President Trump suggested a US-Iran war would end "very soon," with oil prices "tumbling down," though Iran's IRGC Spokesman warned Trump to learn lessons from the Iran war and accept its conditions. Concurrently, a Flydubai co-pilot attempted an axe attack on an Israel-bound flight, which UAE officials and prosecution have labeled a "terrorist act." The co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, was reportedly barred from flying in his native Oman over security and extremism concerns. Netanyahu warned of a "very heavy price" if any power was behind the incident, while an Israeli investigation team arrived in the Emirates, assessing the co-pilot acted alone.

Brazilian Election: Brazil is on the eve of a high-stakes presidential election, featuring a rematch between President Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro, with some Brazilians viewing it as a vote on President Trump's influence, as Trump claims success in winning races in Latin America. The US has been accused of election interference, while crime is a top concern for voters, reflecting a broader rightward shift across Latin America.

Global Economy: The G7 nations, under increased pressure from Washington, announced they will release 100 million reserve barrels of oil and diesel fuel over the next four months following an emergency meeting on energy. This move aims to address global energy market pressures.

European Protests: Across Europe, significant domestic challenges persist, with France arresting 5,000 people, mostly teens, amid spreading school protests over overcrowded classrooms and teacher shortages. In Spain, tens of thousands protested nationwide after lawmakers rejected measures aimed at strengthening tenant protection and making housing more affordable, following the eviction of an 87-year-old woman. Meanwhile, Germany's political center is grappling for relevance after recent electoral gains by the far right and far left.

Regional Conflicts: Escalating conflicts continue to destabilize various regions. In Yemen, Houthi rebels claim to have struck an Aramco oil facility near Riyadh, while accusing Saudi forces of launching dozens of strikes on Sanaa, prompting the Yemeni army to claim it targeted Houthis, killing 700. Ethiopian government forces have retaken the airport in Tigray's capital, Mekelle, with rebels abandoning the city, as fighting threatens to spill into conflicts in the wider Horn of Africa. Meanwhile, a Palestinian child was killed by an Israeli strike in Gaza, while Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian vehicles in the occupied West Bank and attempted to set a Palestinian child on fire.
